prompt: Context: I'm building a modular 3D architecture kit for the Anchorkin, a culture of huge stone-and-chain folk in a stylized painterly high-fantasy sky-island game. Attached: images 1-3 (market town, airship, world-tree isle) are the LOCKED rendering style: painterly, hand-painted, chunky readable forms, warm soft light. Images 4-8 (Ledger wall landmark, dwellings, civic chain forge, outpost blockhouse, props) are the APPROVED Anchorkin concept designs that the kit must be able to rebuild. Kit grid: 3 m horizontal module, 4 m storey, walls 1 m thick and battered 8 degrees inward, doors 2 x 3.2 m. Materials: dark basalt and slate with teal crystal veins, black forged iron, giant chain links, carved Ledger inscription bands, oath-marks carved on doorposts. IMPORTANT correction to the concept dwellings: they came out as ordinary pitched-roof stone cottages. The kit must push a horizontal, squat, stepped, battered-wall silhouette with low flat or shallow stepped stone roofs and terraces, never steep slate gables. I will ask for 5 kit reference sheets, one image each, all following these KIT-SHEET RULES (different from the concept sheets): wide landscape image; orthographic front elevation of each piece plus a small three-quarter view beside it; isolated pieces only, no scenery, no floating rock, no sky; light neutral grey background with faint module grid lines and a small dimension label under each piece (e.g. "3 x 4 m"); one human-height figure about 2.6 m tall (an Anchorkin, they are huge) standing beside the pieces for scale; consistent flat even studio light, softer and less sepia than the concept sheets; painterly hand-painted surfaces with chunky readable forms. Generate sheet 1 now as an image, title "Anchorkin Kit - Structure": plinth, slope step, cliff-edge foundation with iron chain anchors, battered walls (plain, window opening, door opening, half-height, end cap, Ledger-band wall), outer corner, inner corner, buttress column, floor tile, terrace step, straight stairs. Each wall piece exactly one 3 m module wide and one 4 m storey tall, with the 8 degree inward batter clearly visible in the front views.
